newsitem.title: USA: Texas Stock Index sets record in May - Comptroller.
newsitem.headline: Texas Stock Index sets record in May - Comptroller.

text.p: A month after hitting the 300 mark for the first time, the Texas Stock Index smashed April's record, shooting up to 356.8 in May, a release from State Comptroller John Sharp's office said.
"After rising 21.8 points in April, the TSI climbed another 46.6 points in May," Sharp said. "The index is 53.4 percent higher than one year ago."

By comparison, the Standard & Poor's 500, which uses a nationwide sampling of stock prices, climbed 47 points in May. On a percentage basis, the S&P 500 rose 5.9 percent, while the TSI rose 15 percent, the release said.

Texas technology companies did especially well in May, with stock values soaring 240.2 points, or 28.7 percent. Overall, Texas technology stock prices are up 143.2 percent compared to a year ago. Texas Instruments Inc stock rose after the company announced that it won a $98.3 million contract to produce infrared imaging technology for the U.S. Army.

The State Comptroller's office produces the monthly TSI to help measure investor confidence in Texas-based businesses. TSI is one of 10 components of the Index of Leading Texas Economic Indicators, which Sharp's office also produces.
